title: Typed feature acceptance vs control evidence
root_cause: Operational transition logic can accept green child-control evidence while a required runtime feature is explicitly missing.
source_requirement: Make feature acceptance typed, revision-bound, and distinct from control-interaction evidence.
implementation_steps: Enforce required-runtime-feature and authority-class checks in reconciliation and transition admission.
Make completion projection consume accepted feature claims only.
Bind evidence freshness to source and dependency revisions.
negative_cases: Green UI control with missing runtime feature.
Contained/local receipt offered for real external claim.
Evidence bound to stale source revision.
Child control N/A offered as parent feature N/A.
focused_tests: tests/test_operational_gap_ledger.py - transition admission and reconciliation cases
evidence_required: Focused negative vectors and affected-section receipts at the changed revision.
rollback: Restore prior acceptance functions and discard only newly generated current projections.
acceptance_criteria: A green control cannot prove missing runtime behavior.
Real external claims reject contained evidence.
Stale source revisions invalidate feature evidence.

status_history.evidence: 100 focused tests passed; 393 downstream tests passed with one skip and 12 subtests
Fresh impact mapping expanded the release-artifact compatibility cone to 58 tests; downstream closure is withheld until that cone passes.
